findings: jpiquot@local already targets https://192.168.1.30:6443; node1 has that internal IP.
No cert-manager Certificate in any namespace targets openbao/openbao-server-tls. No namespace-local Issuer in openbao.

ClusterIssuer openbao-internal-pki is Ready and uses pki-int/sign/hexalith-memories-services with Kubernetes auth role cert-manager-internal-pki, ServiceAccount cert-manager/openbao-pki-issuer and transport CA reference openbao-client-ca/ca.crt.
The ClusterIssuer inline caBundle is empty. The attempted decoder failed; no CA fingerprint was established from that attempt. The referenced Secret was not read.

Public CA-verifying read of pki-int/cert/ca returns Hexalith Internal Intermediate CA issued by Hexalith Internal Root CA, distinct in identity from the previously inventoried listener issuer Hexalith Keys Internal CA. This discovers an application PKI, not an authoritative renewal procedure for the current server leaf.
HCL ownership shows Helm plus kubectl modification managers; their names/timestamps do not identify the certificate issuer or an external source repository.
No KubeSphere ApplicationRelease or app.k8s.io Application objects returned. API discovery returned no Flux/ArgoCD/ExternalSecrets resource type.
The named TLS/PKI Secrets exist, but their contents, annotations and managedFields were not queried under the inherited names/types-only Secret restriction.
